title: Fed Holds, Long-End Yields Climb and a Firm Dollar as Central-Bank Divergence Widens
content: A hawkish rates and FX regime dominated the window. Sticky US inflation kept the Fed on hold at its 29 July meeting, a fourth consecutive pause in the 3.50-3.75% range, and prompted markets to trim 2026 rate-cut bets. The long end bore the strain: the 10-year UST yield pushed towards 4.65% and the 30-year above 5.15%, steepening the curve as fiscal and term-premium concerns lingered. Policy divergence widened the gap, with the ECB holding at 2.4% on cautious guidance while several other central banks tilted towards holds or hikes, leaving the USD firm. EUR/USD slipped towards 1.13 and the yen languished near multi-decade lows. The regime intermittently pressured rate-sensitive equities and gold, making every inflation and labour print pivotal for cross-asset direction.

title: Megacap AI Leadership Whipsaws From a Semi Rout Back to Record Highs on Strong Earnings
content: AI-linked megacaps again drove the tape, but with sharply two-sided volatility. Early in the window the semiconductor complex extended a violent reversal into bear-market territory on AI-capex scepticism and soft chip guidance, dragging Asian names lower and unsettling breadth. Sentiment then flipped as second-quarter results landed: Microsoft jumped around 16% on accelerating Azure growth, Amazon surged, and chipmakers rebounded hard, with Micron and AMD posting double-digit gains. The S&P 500 climbed back to fresh records near 7,440 and the Dow logged a fourth straight monthly advance. The episode underscored extreme index concentration, with a handful of names dictating direction and elevated hedging demand. For investors it kept positioning, breadth and the durability of AI infrastructure spending at the centre of the equity narrative.
